newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower in sluggish trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower in a narrow consolidaiton on Wednesday on what brokers called directionless trade before a three-day-long weekend.
The weighted index lost 39.33 points or 0.61 percent to end at 6,438.52 points on turnover of T$40.14 billion.
"Pre-holiday selling pressure has not finished. People could not find a direction in the market," said Mike Tsai of Grand Cathay Securities.
Brokers noted continued selling from many firms to raise cash to pay bonuses or buy gifts for employees and clients for Friday's Mid-Autumn festival, a major Taiwan holiday.
Taiwan's financial markets will be closed on Friday and Saturday for the festival.
Chiao Tung Bank soared by the daily seven percent limit on its first day of listing on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. The firm, topping the gainers' list, was limit up, surging T$4 to T$58.5.
The market was hoping the listing of Chiao Tung Bank could give a boost to the heavily weighted financial sector and the main market, brokers said.
Blue chip electronics drew minor buying, with Mosel up 60 cents or 1.70 percent to T$35.9 and Acer Inc up 60 cents or 1.48 percent to T$41.2.
Plastics and textiles were weak, down 1.31 percent and 1.52 percent respectively. China Steel, the second most active issue, fell 40 cents or 1.56 percent to T$25.3.
Brokers expected the market to move around the current levels on Thursday.

"It's safe to say there will be no major movements until after the Mid-Autumn Festival," said Albert Lin of Golden Securities. He added several new investment trust funds were expected to enter the market next week.
A range of 6,400-6,500 was seen for Thursday.
